max_tire.size: 33 in (e.g. 285/70R17); 35 in on Rubicon with bump-stop spacers
max_tire.note: A 35 clears a Rubicon at ride height but rubs the inner fenders on compression and at full lock. Bump-stop extensions fix it at the cost of about 2 in of up-travel. On Sport and Sahara, a 33 is the sensible stock limit.

Jeep's factory Xtreme 35 package for the two-door from 2024, on Rubicon and Willys with the 2.0 turbo only ($4,495): 1.5 in lift, 4.56 gears, 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels and a reinforced swing gate. Standard on the 2.0T two-door Rubicon X.
What Sport and Sahara need for 35s, together with bump stops and a wheel with about 4.5–5.0 in backspacing.

items.title: Front track bar bracket welds (the 'frame weld' recall)
items.summary: Track bar brackets may be improperly welded and separate from the frame, reducing steering capability; dealers inspect and repair the welds.

items.title: Intermediate steering shaft weld
items.summary: The shaft may not have been properly welded and can split, so the wheel loses centre (recall U48).

items.title: Rear underbody ladder rail corrosion
items.summary: The rail can corrode, weakening the rear floor and loosening the left rear seat mount; dealers apply rust protection (recall U27, 106 vehicles).

items.title: Steering column stub shaft
items.summary: Improperly machined stub shafts can break and detach the steering wheel (recall V29).

items.title: Manual-transmission clutch pressure plate
items.summary: Pressure plate may overheat and fracture (recall W12).

items.title: Clutch overheating software
items.summary: Expansion of the clutch pressure-plate overheating recall to 2018–2021 manual trucks.

items.title: Clutch assembly replacement
items.summary: Further expansion to 2018–2023 manual trucks (pressure plate may overheat and fracture); 24V-572 re-flashes some 2021 trucks already remedied under it, because the new software could stall the engine.

items.title: Left lower control arm bracket weld
items.summary: Bracket and weld may be mispositioned (recall W01, 3,005 vehicles).

items.title: Frame stud can puncture fuel tank
items.summary: In a crash a frame stud may puncture the tank (recall 28A).

items.title: Instrument cluster short
items.summary: The cluster can short internally and fail (recall 30B).

items.title: Electric-hydraulic power steering pump wiring fire
items.summary: Pump wiring can overheat and start a fire even when parked; owners told to park outside until repaired (1,076,999 vehicles across Wrangler and Gladiator).

tsbs.title: Death wobble: steering damper replacement
tsbs.summary: About 192,000 2018–2019 JLs get a new front steering damper for a sustained steering-wheel shimmy after bumps, especially above 55 mph and below 40°F. It's a customer satisfaction notification, not a safety recall.

tsbs.title: Steering-wheel shimmy after road irregularities
tsbs.summary: November 2019 bulletin for 2018–2020 JL (and 2020 Gladiator) that points technicians to a diagnosis and repair video for the steering linkage and damper.

timeline.change: JL launch (four-door production from November 2017, two-door from early 2018): 3.6 Pentastar with a 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto, plus a 2.0 turbo with eTorque (auto only). Early trucks need the track-bar weld, steering-shaft and V41 damper fixes.
3.0 EcoDiesel V6 (260 hp) arrives, four-door only; later subject to high-pressure fuel pump recalls

Wrangler 4xe plug-in hybrid (375 hp, 21-mile EV range) and Rubicon 392 (6.4 Hemi, 470 hp), both four-door only. Xtreme Recon package (35s, 4.56 gears, 1.5 in lift) for the four-door Rubicon and 392; 4.88 axles optional on Rubicon.
Facelift: new grille (except Sport/Sport S), standard 12-inch Uconnect 5, new Rubicon X trim. Xtreme 35 package reaches the two-door. EcoDiesel dropped. Rubicon 392 'Final Edition'.
Rubicon 392 continues, still badged 'Final Edition'; Stellantis drops the 4xe from the US market (Wikipedia)
Moab 392 tops the range (four-door only); reworked door hinges for easier removal; 3.6 still offered with the manual; no 4xe in the US

identify.intro: Two-door JLs come with three powertrains and two very different axle packages, and the big-ticket hardware (4xe, 392, EcoDiesel) was four-door only.

items.head: Real Rubicon
items.body: Dana M210 (44-class) front and M220 rear with Tru-Lok electronic lockers, Rock-Trac with 4:1 low range, and an electronic sway-bar disconnect. Sport and Sahara have the M186 ('Dana 30') front and M200 ('Dana 35') rear, with an optional limited slip, and Command-Trac with 2.72:1 (Selec-Trac optional on Sahara).

items.head: Factory 35s
items.body: Factory Xtreme 35 trucks (2.0T two-door Rubicon and Willys from 2024; standard on the 2.0T two-door Rubicon X) have LT315/70R17 BFGoodrich KO2s on 17x8 beadlock-capable wheels, 4.56 gears, a 1.5 in lift and a reinforced swing gate.

items.head: Engine
items.body: The 3.6 Pentastar comes with the 6-speed manual or 8-speed auto. The 2.0 turbo is auto-only. There was never a two-door 4xe, 392 or EcoDiesel.

items.head: Pre- or post-facelift
items.body: 2024-on trucks have the 12-inch Uconnect 5 screen with horizontal dash vents. All but Sport and Sport S also get the new grille.

items.head: JL vs JK at a glance
items.body: The JL's headlights cut into the grille, the spare sits lower and the Jeep logo is no longer on the grille.

capability.note: 2018 Sport to Rubicon; 12.6 in (320 mm) with the 2024 Xtreme 35 package
2018 Rubicon; 34 in with the 2024 Xtreme 35 package

values.intro: Two-door JLs hold value well. Late Rubicons and factory-35 trucks sit near the top, while early Sports are the cheapest way into a JL.

ranges.cond: Late / low-mile Rubicon X or modified

values.note: Based on about 15 two-door JL sales on Bring a Trailer in 2025–26; a 2024 Rubicon X brought $46,000.
